items.title: Michael Olise
items.description: Michael Olise est un joueur français né en Angleterre le 12 décembre 2001. Capable d'évoluer sur une aile, en numéro 10 à l'ancienne ou derrière l'attaquant de pointe, il joue au Bayern Munich depuis 2024. Avant ça, il avait fait toutes ses gammes dans le foot anglais, faisant ses débuts professionnels à Reading, avant de rejoindre Crystal Palace. Il a choisi de porter les couleurs de l'équipe de France, pays de sa mère. C'est le 6 septembre 2024 qu'il a honoré sa première sélection avec les Bleus de Didier Deschamps, avant de devenir petit à petit un indispensable. Jusqu'à éblouir tout le monde à la Coupe du monde 2026.

items.title: Lineker debutó con un doblete al Racing
items.description: Gary Lineker vistió en tres temporadas la camiseta del Barça: llegó al Camp Nou en 1986 procedente del Everton con el cartel de máximo goleador del Mundial de aquel verano, y se fue en 1989 al Tottenham. En aquellas tres campañas, el delantero británico marcó un total de 52 goles en partidos oficiales, 4 de ellos de penalti. Y no pudo empezar mejor: en su debut contra el Racing de Santander firmó un ‘doblete’ y se bastó para dejar él solo, en apenas 26 minutos, el 2-0 en el marcador con el que finalizó el encuentro.

items.description: El nivel de una plantilla también se ve en su número de internacionales. Edin Terzic no ha podido trabajar esta semana con siete de sus futbolistas porque están con sus selecciones. Tres con España, la campeona del mundo, y los tres con un papel muy relevante en la obtención del título. Unai Simón y Laporte fueron titulares indiscutibles en el torneo celebrado en verano y Nico Williams fue decisivo en la final. Cuando un equipo tiene a tres campeones del mundo siendo importantes por algo es.

items.title: El 'nudo' del Manchester United
items.description: Cualquier analista económico que analizara las finanzas del Manchester United diría hoy que es un club asfixiado económicamente y en una extraña paradoja operativa. Sigue siendo, con su prestigio, una máquina de generar ingresos comerciales, pero está lastrado por una estructura de deuda acumulada, heredada de décadas de mala y cuestionable gestión, que consume su liquidez y limita su margen de maniobra deportivo. Una ‘tenaza’ financiera que le estrecha y maniata frente a sus grandes rivales ingleses. Esa es la cruda realidad --los ‘números rojos’—con que reciben al nuevo entrenador, Mauricio Pochettino, el octavo técnico permanente desde el 2013, que llega en sustitución de Michael Carrick.

items.title: Matarazzo busca al extremo que haga de Barrene
items.description: Es momento de mirar hacia delante. El parón permite además tener unos días más para planificar y pensar, en el caso de staff y dirección deportiva, qué hacer tras la grave lesión de Barrenetxea. Alguien tendrá que hacer de Barrene y ocupar su lugar en el ‘once’, en la rotación, y no solo de la manera más simple, sino también aportando como él hace. Evidentemente la opción de mirar al mercado invernal está abierta y Bretos y sus scouts están en la obligación de estar preparados para ello. Pero, incluso en caso afirmativo sobre si lo ideal es fichar a alguien, quedan aún nueve partidos en 2026 en apenas 28 días que exigirán un plus a la Real, a Matarazzo y, en este caso concreto, a los extremos realistas. Primero hay que buscar dentro, entre lo que hay. Que no es poco. Y conviene tener en cuenta que el entrenador hasta ahora viene defendiendo con línea de cinco, usando a uno de los extremos atrás, que era siempre que estaba sobre el verde, Barrene. No todos valen para eso.

items.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
items.description: The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearanceHappy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue. items.title: Lionel Scaloni’s renewal puts him on course to break a historic record as Argentina coach
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030 opens the door for him to surpass legends like Menotti and Bilardo and write his name in Argentina’s history books. 
Lionel Scaloni’s renewal does not only secure Argentina’s coach for the next cycle, it also opens the door to making history from the bench. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) confirmed on Thursday, through its president Claudio Tapia, that the coach will continue through 2030, and has put him on course for a mark that no Argentine coach has achieved before.



If Scaloni remains in charge until the 2030 World Cup, he will become the first coach to lead Argentina at three World Cups: Qatar 2022, the 2026 edition in North America, and the Centenary World Cup in 2030.



In doing so, he would surpass the marks of César Luis Menotti, who coached the team in 1978 and 1982, and Carlos Bilardo, who did so in 1986 and 1990, both with two tournaments each.



The record comes after a 2026 World Cup that ended in heartbreak, with Argentina losing the final against Spain on July 19, a result that left his continuity in doubt. “The blow of not having won the final was hard, and the first thing that comes to your mind is to think about what to do, see what comes and try to recharge your batteries,” Scaloni explained at the final press conference.




Lionel Scaloni, chasing more moments like this. 🥹🇦🇷 #FIFAWorldCup pic.twitter.com/xbCvokDiDr— FIFA World Cup (@FIFAWorldCup) November 12, 2026




Almost four months after the final at MetLife Stadium, Scaloni has finally decided to accept the offer to stay on as coach and will look to keep making history with Argentina.



Scaloni’s résumé: the records he holds and the ones he chases


        


Few coaches have built a case as strong as Scaloni’s. In 107 matches in charge of Argentina, he has recorded 79 wins, 18 draws, and 10 losses, and he has won four official titles: the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup, and the 2024 Copa America. That puts him in second place among Argentina’s most successful coaches by trophies, tied with Alfio Basile and behind Guillermo Stabile, who won seven.



Some of those marks already belong to him. Scaloni is the coach who has directed the most World Cup matches (13) and won the most (10) in Argentina’s history and he also led the team through a 36-game unbeaten streak between 2019 and 2022, which surpassed the previous record of 31 held by Basile’s team. The run only ended in the opening match of the Qatar World Cup, a 2-1 loss to Saudi Arabia.



Stabile’s numbers, however, remain within reach. Scaloni needs five more wins to become the coach with the most victories in the history of the national team and he needs 18 more matches to surpass the 124 that Stabile directed, something he could achieve as early as the 2028 Copa America.



With his contract now running through 2030, Scaloni has the time and the tournaments to turn those pursuits into reality. To match Stabile’s seven titles, he would need to win the 2028 Copa America and the 2030 World Cup, and also the Finalissima against Spain, a title that for now remains pending.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni reveals decision on Lionel Messi’s No. 10 after renewing with Argentina
items.description:
One of the first questions of Argentina’s new era is who will inherit the No. 10 shirt left vacant by Lionel Messi. After the Argentine Football Association confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, the coach addressed the subject at a press conference in Buenos Aires, ahead of Friday’s friendly against Uruguay at La Bombonera. Scaloni […] 
One of the first questions of Argentina’s new era is who will inherit the No. 10 shirt left vacant by Lionel Messi. After the Argentine Football Association confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, the coach addressed the subject at a press conference in Buenos Aires, ahead of Friday’s friendly against Uruguay at La Bombonera.



Scaloni made it clear that, for now, the shirt will not have a new owner. “In this match we won’t give it to anyone. We haven’t thought about who we’ll give it to when it becomes obligatory,” he said, meaning that, at least for this FIFA window, nobody will wear the No. 10.



He did explain, however, what he would like to happen when that moment arrives. “We hope that the day we do it, it’s forever, and that we don’t keep changing it. The idea is to give it to the player who can keep it,” Scaloni said, which suggests that the number will be reserved for a player who can wear it for years, as Messi did.



The obligation comes from FIFA, which requires national teams in official competitions to number their squads consecutively from 1 to 23, so the No. 10 cannot simply be skipped and must be assigned to a specific player. That means Scaloni will eventually have to decide who wears it, although for now he insists the matter is not something that worries him.




#SelecciónMayor La historia continúa… pic.twitter.com/Wv4oCKpCuU— 🇦🇷 Selección Argentina ⭐⭐⭐ (@Argentina) November 12, 2026




Scaloni on life without Messi: ‘I hope he’s happy’



Even without Messi in the squad, his name was present throughout Scaloni’s press conference. When the coach was asked how Argentina will play without him, he was clear about what it means for the team’s identity. “There’s no way to try to play without him; now we’ll try to play a similar game but with different alternatives,” Scaloni said, acknowledging that the style will not change, but the players who carry it out will.


        


He also admitted that he has not yet discussed his renewal with his former captain. “I haven’t spoken with Leo, I hope he’s happy that we can continue,” Scaloni said, a comment that shows how much of the project still revolves around Messi’s approval.



For the coach, however, the next step is to build on what is already in place. “It’s an advantage that we have players who already know us, but this is football and what matters is that those who come adapt as soon as possible to what we want, which is what this is about: getting to know each other and training together,” he explained.



With the No. 10 shirt still without an owner and Messi’s reaction to his renewal still unknown, Scaloni begins his new cycle on Friday against Uruguay at La Bombonera. The match will be the first real chance to see how Argentina’s style holds up, with younger players and without the player who defined the last era.

items.title: Argentina confirm Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030 as new era begins without Lionel Messi
items.description:
Argentina confirmed Lionel Scaloni’s renewal through 2030, with a new era starting without Lionel Messi and a change in the coach’s team. 
Argentina has secured its coach for the next cycle just as it begins a new chapter without Lionel Messi. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) confirmed on Thursday that Lionel Scaloni will continue at the helm of the national team through 2030.



The announcement was made by AFA president Claudio Tapia during a press conference in Ezeiza, alongside the coach himself. “It’s a very special day for the Argentine national team and Argentine soccer. We’re going to officially announce the renewal of Lionel Scaloni for the period 2027 to 2030,” Tapia told reporters.



The coach said his motivation is the same as when he took charge in 2018. “We have the same hope and desire as the first day, otherwise it would be impossible to be here,” Scaloni explained. He also said that this will be a new era after Messi’s departure, in which new players will emerge. “A new era begins, we will give a chance to kids who are pushing from behind,” he added.



The extension is a reward for a cycle that has brought four official titles since his arrival: the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup, and the 2024 Copa America.




𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐒𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐢 𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐥 𝟐𝟎𝟑𝟎 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/3W3O5xEvI5— Selección Argentina in English (@AFASeleccionEN) November 12, 2026




Across 107 matches, Scaloni has recorded 79 wins, 18 draws, and 10 losses, and his first test of this new stage will come right away, in the friendlies against Uruguay on Friday at La Bombonera and Costa Rica next Tuesday in Cordoba.



Walter Samuel leaves Scaloni’s coaching staff


        


The renewal comes with one change in the coach’s team, as Walter Samuel will leave the national team’s staff after eight years by Scaloni’s side. The coach himself made it official at the press conference: “Walter Samuel, as I had already advanced, will start his career alone. Eternal gratitude to a friend, I wish him the best because he was an important part of our staff and it’s fair that he can begin his path”.



Samuel will still be on the bench for both of those matches, which will be his last. The former Real Madrid defender had been part of the staff since the beginning of the cycle in 2018, alongside Pablo Aimar, and his specific role was set pieces and the defensive side of the team.



The coach also made clear that, for now, there will be no replacement for Samuel. “In principle we won’t add anyone. We believe we can continue like this and that’s what we’re going to try. We stay as we are,” Scaloni said, although he did not rule out changes later on: “In any case, we have people in youth who could give us a hand, and that would be in the future”.



With Samuel’s departure and a new generation knocking at the door, Scaloni begins this new cycle with the same group of collaborators but a very different roster. Argentina’s next challenge will be to show that the project can keep winning without Messi, starting with the Uruguay friendly on Friday.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement adds emotional twist to son’s Portugal U-17 debut as teenager comes close to dream first goal
items.description:
While the legendary forward has brought his international career to an end, his 16-year-old son has taken another important step towards following in his footsteps, attracting attention during a memorable appearance for the youth national team. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and his eldest son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., have reached two very different milestones in Portugal’s soccer history within the space of a week. While the legendary forward has brought his international career to an end, his 16-year-old son has taken another important step towards following in his footsteps, attracting attention during a memorable appearance for the youth national team.



Ronaldo Jr. made his Portugal Under-17 debut on Thursday, featuring in a European Championship qualifying match against Andorra. The occasion carried additional significance because of who was watching from the stands and the timing of his father’s recent announcement.



The young Selecao secured a comfortable 4-0 victory over Andorra at Cidade do Futebol in Oeiras, making a positive start to its Under-17 European Championship qualifying campaign. Diego Farinha scored twice, while Kaua Miranda converted a penalty and Rafael Cabral added another goal in the second half.



Ronaldo Jr. entered the match as a substitute in the 73rd minute, replacing Victor Bastianele with the result already effectively decided. Wearing the number 18 shirt, the Al-Nassr academy forward had limited time to make an impression but still came close to marking his debut with a goal.



Moments Cristiano Jr got subbed on.Portugal U17 are 4–0 up against Andorra.🇵🇹🇦🇩 pic.twitter.com/YgRDbvy3Ck— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 12, 2026 



The teenager comes close to memorable first goal



The biggest opportunity arrived late in the match when Ronaldo Jr. connected with a cross from the left inside the penalty area. His header narrowly missed the target, denying him a dream start at Under-17 level and leaving Portugal’s scoreline unchanged.



The teenager’s physical presence was already noticeable, although he still has plenty of time to develop as a player. His latest appearance represents another stage in an international journey that has already included spells with Portugal’s Under-15 and Under-16 teams.



¡CÓMO NO RECORDARTE! 🥹Cristiano Jr. debutó con la Selección Sub-17 de Portugal y nos hizo acordarnos del Bicho 🐐🇵🇹(Vía X: mousaqi/Sporting) pic.twitter.com/ojYfUv0UET— ESPN.com.mx (@ESPNmx) November 12, 2026 



Portugal’s senior stars watch Ronaldo’s son make his debut



The occasion became even more emotional because members of the Selecao’s senior national team were reportedly present to watch the youth side in action. Players including Vitinha, Joao Cancelo, Joao Felix and Joao Neves were among those following the match at the national training center.



Their presence created a memorable connection between Portugal’s established stars and the next generation. However, one particularly important figure was missing from the occasion: Ronaldo himself, who had announced his international retirement only a week earlier.



The Portuguese National Team players watching the U17 game.Cristiano Ronaldo would have been present to watch his son play, if he hadn't retired.🥲 pic.twitter.com/jZ2s0OdIiq— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) November 12, 2026 



The timing prompted an emotional reaction from soccer fans, with social media users highlighting what the moment might have looked like had the veteran forward remained available for Portugal.



What comes next for Ronaldo Jr. and Portugal U-17?



Portugal’s qualifying campaign continues with upcoming matches against Bulgaria and Serbia, scheduled for November 14 and November 17, respectively. Those fixtures will give Ronaldo Jr. further opportunities to earn minutes and establish himself at this level.



His debut against Andorra may have lasted only around 17 minutes, but it represented an important personal milestone. With his father stepping away from international soccer, the teenager now has the opportunity to create his own story in the same national colors, with the support of some of Portugal’s biggest stars.

items.title: Czechia vs Spain: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Czechia vs Spain in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Czechia and Spain meet again just days after their last meeting, and this time the venue flips with Czechia hosting in this Nations League fixture.
Czechia have lost all three of their recent matches, falling 0-3 to England on October 6, 1-3 to Spain on October 3, and 0-2 to England on September 29. The run has left them without a win across this stretch, and a result against Spain would offer a rare lift after back-to-back shutout defeats to England sandwiched around the first meeting with this same opponent. For Czechia, the game is really about stopping the bleeding before the next camp.
Spain, by contrast, arrive on the back of three straight wins, beating Croatia 2-1 on October 6, Czechia 3-1 on October 3, and Croatia 4-1 on September 29. That stretch has them scoring freely and conceding little, with nine goals put away across the three games. A repeat result here would extend the momentum and confirm Spain as the form side of this Nations League group.
Czechia confirmed lineup
Czechia are set up in a 4-2-3-1, with Antonín Kinský behind a back line of Vladimír Coufal, Štěpán Chaloupek, Ladislav Krejčí and Jiří Sláma. Tomáš Souček and Alex Král look to anchor midfield, giving the side some physical presence in front of the defense, while Kryštof Daněk, Lukáš Ambros and Lukáš Červ support Adam Hložek as the central striker. There are no listed absences, so this looks like close to a full-strength selection, but the group still has to find a way to defend better after conceding five goals in two matches against England and three more against Spain earlier this month.
Czechia confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Matěj Kovář, Vladimír Coufal, David Jurásek, Alex Král, David Zima, Ladislav Krejčí, Lukáš Ambros, Lukáš Červ, Ryan Naderi, Adam Hložek, Lukáš Provod. Coach: Santi Denia.
Spain confirmed lineup
Spain line up in the same 4-2-3-1 shape, with Unai Simón in goal behind Pedro Porro, Pau Cubarsí, Dean Huijsen and Alex Grimaldo. Fabián Ruiz and Martín Zubimendi sit in the double pivot, and Fermín López joins Jorge De Frutos and Álex Baena behind Ferran Torres in attack. Coach Luis De La Fuente has no reported absences to work around, and the continuity in personnel reflects a team that has scored at least two goals in each of its last three outings.
Spain confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Unai Simón, Pedro Porro, Marc Cucurella, Fabián Ruiz, Pau Cubarsí, Dean Huijsen, Yéremy Pino, Martín Zubimendi, Ferran Torres, Fermín López, Álex Baena. Coach: Luis de la Fuente.

items.title: Why is Bukayo Saka not playing for England vs Croatia in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
England will face Croatia at Wembley without one of their most important attackers. Bukayo Saka, the Arsenal winger who has been Thomas Tuchel’s first choice on the right flank, is still recovering from a quad injury and will not be available for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, nor for the rest of […] 
England will face Croatia at Wembley without one of their most important attackers. Bukayo Saka, the Arsenal winger who has been Thomas Tuchel’s first choice on the right flank, is still recovering from a quad injury and will not be available for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, nor for the rest of the international break.



Saka suffered the injury after just 10 minutes of Arsenal’s Champions League match against Bayern Munich last month, and he has since missed Arsenal’s last five games.



There were initial fears that he could be out for up to eight weeks, but Mikel Arteta has been cautiously optimistic about his recovery. “The way it happened, it wasn’t a really aggressive action,” the Arsenal manager said ahead of the win over Hull on Nov. 7.



“So that gives you some hope as well that the tissue will repair in a more efficient and faster way as well and he has some very good symptoms right now. So we have to wait and see,” the Spanish coach concluded about Saka’s recovery, as the winger still has no confirmed return date.



"Unfortunately he's going to be out for a while"Mikel Arteta provides an injury update on Bukayo Saka 🏥 pic.twitter.com/pOyzd8csM8— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 6, 2026 



The absence comes at a decisive moment for England, who have won three of their four Nations League games without conceding a goal, and whose only loss was a 3-2 defeat at Wembley against Spain in late September.



A draw against Croatia would be enough to guarantee a place in the quarterfinals, while top spot in the group will be decided on Sunday in Madrid, where Tuchel’s side will face Spain without Saka again.


        


Who will replace Saka on England’s right wing?



Tuchel has already identified who will try to fill the gap left by Saka. “I think it’s Morgan Rogers for us and then it will be Rio [Ngumoha] on that side. He played there for Liverpool and impressed in the last camp,” the England coach said, naming the Chelsea forward as the likeliest to start on the right against Croatia, with Ngumoha as the alternative.



He also mentioned other possibilities: “Josh King can maybe play there, we will try this, and then Morgan Gibbs-White can play on the wing. We need runners there who can attack through the lines, so I think we have options”.



The options are also reduced because Noni Madueke, who deputized for Saka at the World Cup in the summer, was left out of the squad. Tuchel admitted that the decision was not easy: “It’s a close call and difficult decision not to bring Noni, but we stick with the group that we had and give them our trust”.



Whoever gets the nod on Thursday will face a double challenge, because Saka will also be absent on Sunday against Spain, a match that could decide who finishes first in the group. For Tuchel, the performance of his replacement against Croatia could therefore be an indication of how England will approach the next game without one of their key attackers.

items.title: Why is Lamine Yamal not playing for Spain vs Czechia in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5?
items.description:
Luis de la Fuente’s side will travel to Prague looking to maintain its impressive run and strengthen its position at the top of Group A3, although the Barcelona youngster will be missing from the squad for a reason that has attracted considerable attention. 
Lamine Yamal’s absence is set to be one of the biggest talking points when Spain faces Czechia in its 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 5 clash. Luis de la Fuente’s side will travel to Prague looking to maintain its impressive run and strengthen its position at the top of Group A3, although the Barcelona youngster will be missing from the squad for a reason that has attracted considerable attention.



Spain has dominated Group A3, winning all four of its opening matches to secure qualification for the quarter-finals. The reigning world champion has collected 12 points, scoring 12 goals along the way, and currently sits three points ahead of England.



De la Fuente’s side began the campaign with a memorable 3-2 victory over England before beating Croatia 4-1 and Czechia 3-1. La Roja then completed another win over Croatia, 2-1, and will now aim to extend its impressive winning streak before facing England in its final group match.



Spain has also enjoyed an excellent run across all competitions, winning its last 11 matches. Its opponent, meanwhile, has struggled throughout the campaign and has yet to collect a single point.



Victor Munoz of Spain shoots and misses vs Czechia



Czechia face uphill battle against the world champion



Czechia has lost all four of its Nations League fixtures, leaving it bottom of Group A3 and facing the possibility of relegation to League B. Its defeats include losses to Croatia and England at home, followed by a 3-1 defeat against Spain and a 3-0 setback at Wembley.



The national team has also lost five consecutive matches across all competitions, with its last victory coming in a friendly against Guatemala in June. Although Czechia can still finish third, stopping Spain will be a difficult task given the visitors’ current form and their dominant record in this fixture.



PositionTeamPlayedW-D-LPoints1.Spain44-0-0122.England43-0-193.Croatia41-0-334.Czechia40-0-40UEFA Nations League A – Group 3 Standings



Spain has won six of its eight previous meetings with Czechia, while the other two ended in draws. Czechia has never beaten La Roja, adding another challenge for Santi Denia’s team ahead of Thursday’s encounter.



Why Lamine Yamal is missing against Czechia



The reason behind Yamal’s absence is an injury sustained while playing for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid over the weekend. The 19-year-old is nursing a knee problem, which has ruled him out of Spain’s trip to Prague.



According to the reports surrounding the squad announcement, Yamal is expected to join the national team after the Czech Republic fixture and prepare for Sunday’s meeting with England. His absence also allows De la Fuente to manage the workload of one of his most important attacking players.



Lamine Yamal of Spain.



The Spanish teenager has been heavily involved for both the Blaugrana and Spain this season, making his availability an important consideration ahead of the upcoming international fixtures. The decision to leave him out against Czechia also allows the coaching staff to avoid taking unnecessary risks with his fitness.



Yamal is not the only notable absentee for Spain, with Rodri ruled out because of a minor injury, and Mikel Oyarzabal also unavailable because of illness. The forward is another important attacking option for De la Fuente, although his potential return for the England match remains uncertain.

items.title: Toro descubre los órganos de la provincia de Zamora
items.description: "Órganos de la provincia de Zamora" es el título del libro que se presentará el próximo sábado 14 de noviembre, a las 18.30 horas, en el Monasterio del Sancti Spiritus el Real de Toro. Se trata de una publicación del Instituto de Estudios Zamoranos «Florián de Ocampo» (IEZ), institución cultural y de investigación dedicada al estudio, la conservación y la difusión de la historia y la cultura de la provincia de Zamora. La obra recoge la catalogación de los órganos existentes en la provincia, fruto de un exhaustivo trabajo de investigación iniciado en 2020 en el que han participado cuatro especialistas: Fermín Trueba Pérez, Víctor Aliste Izquierdo, Vicente Urones Sánchez y el toresano David García Calvo, bajo la coordinación de Fermín Trueba.

items.title: Football Daily | ‘The club would like to thank …’: Manchester United dust off the heartfelt exit message
items.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Tuesday 22 April 2014: “Manchester United has announced that David Moyes has left the club. The club would like to place on record its thanks for the hard work, honesty and integrity he brought to the role.”Oh no! Where will the USA! USA! USA! ever be able to find a manager who could lead us to the dizzying heights of yet another humiliating defeat in the round of 16? A completely empty safari shirt on a clothes hanger could do that. Now he’s leaving the national team to prioritise a club team, which is exactly what he criticised Christian Pulisic for doing a while back. A $10m dollar buyout from Manchester United is a way more appealing prospect than another World Cup cycle with this guy. Adios, Mauricio. I’d add gracias, but for what, exactly?” – Chi.If any Manchester United fans weren’t already feeling that their board had totally lost its moral compass, then might I suggest that in holding the board meeting to seal Michael Carrick’s fate in Monaco a new bar in tone-deafness has been set. Out of touch, no? Pas du tout. Bonne chance, Mauricio, you are going to need it fella. Meanwhile, let’s pencil in the next board meeting for six months’ time or so. Circus Circus in Las Vegas anyone? Might be too many clowns” – John Collins.With Lil Wayne doing his bit in the jungle, how long before we do actually see Don Pochettino playing a starring role in the Joel & Jim-hosted caper show I’m A Previously Respectable Manager … Get Me Out Of Here?” – Ken Muir.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo deserved better from Portugal as Wesley Sneijder accuses Jorge Jesus of disrespecting CR7 and explains what he should have done
items.description:
The controversy surrounding Jorge Jesus and the former captain has now drawn fresh criticism, raising questions about how a player of Ronaldo’s stature should be treated when his role begins to change. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement continues to generate debate, with former Netherlands midfielder Wesley Sneijder becoming the latest high-profile figure to question how Portugal handled the legendary forward’s final months with the national team. The controversy surrounding Jorge Jesus and the former captain has now drawn fresh criticism, raising questions about how a player of Ronaldo’s stature should be treated when his role begins to change.



Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer on November 5, 2026, bringing a record-breaking 23-year career with Portugal to a close. The 41-year-old finished with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both all-time men’s international records.



His departure followed months of tension surrounding his role under Jesus, who took charge of the Selecao in July 2026. The disagreement became particularly visible during the September international break, when Ronaldo was reportedly sent to warm up during a Nations League match against Norway but was ultimately left on the bench.



The situation reportedly frustrated the forward, who subsequently left the national team camp ahead of Portugal‘s next fixture. He later accepted a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine from the Portuguese Football Federation, with both sanctions expiring before the November internationals.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



Sneijder questions how Jesus handled the situation



The incident has attracted criticism from former players, with Sneijder offering a particularly strong assessment during an appearance on Ziggo Sport’s Rondo. Speaking on the Dutch television program on November 9, the former Real Madrid and Inter midfielder argued that Jesus should have handled the situation privately rather than allowing it to unfold publicly.



His comments were also supported by fellow former Netherlands international Theo Janssen, who described the treatment as “scandalous” and insisted that a player of Ronaldo’s stature deserved greater consideration. The discussion quickly reignited debate over the way Portugal’s coaching staff managed the transition away from its long-time captain.



What Jesus should have done differently, per Sneijder



Sneijder specifically criticized the decision to send Ronaldo out to warm up before leaving him on the bench. He believes Jesus should have spoken directly to the forward before the match and explained his intentions honestly, allowing Ronaldo to understand his role without being placed in an uncomfortable public situation. “Disrespectful. I find it really disrespectful, I really mean that. As a coach you should have sat down with him beforehand. Like: listen, this is how I see it,” Sneijder said.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus



He went further by suggesting that a private conversation over coffee would have prevented the situation from becoming such a public controversy. “You can’t let a moment like the one that has now happened arise, in his very last match. You can’t let that happen!”



Sneijder added: “As a coach you have to be smarter about that, and then you have to say: ‘Listen, let’s go and have a cup of coffee. I’m not going to pick you anymore, how do you feel about that?’”



He concluded that the decision should ultimately have been left in Ronaldo’s hands after an honest discussion. “In the end the ball is with him, right? Then at least you have told him behind the scenes. And then you can work it out together, right?”

items.title: Pep Guardiola’s USMNT dream job could come with problem he never faced at Manchester City as Mauricio Pochettino nears Manchester United move
items.description:
The possibility has generated excitement around the American national team, but convincing the former Manchester City manager to take the job could be only the beginning of a much bigger challenge. 
Pep Guardiola could be heading towards an unexpected return to management, with the United States Soccer Federation reportedly considering him as its leading candidate should Mauricio Pochettino leave the USMNT for Manchester United. The possibility has generated excitement around the American national team, but convincing the former Manchester City manager to take the job could be only the beginning of a much bigger challenge.



Pochettino has emerged as Manchester United’s preferred candidate to replace Michael Carrick, whose team has struggled badly during the current campaign. Reports suggest that discussions surrounding a potential move have gathered pace, although neither Pochettino’s departure nor an agreement with United has been officially confirmed.



The Argentine signed a four-year contract extension with the USMNT in August, committing himself to the project through the 2030 World Cup. Nevertheless, the prospect of returning to the Premier League appears to have created uncertainty over his future, with The Athletic reporting that United has identified him as their chosen candidate if they decide to make a managerial change.



Pochettino was still overseeing the American team’s preparations for its upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti. With the United States’ next competitive fixtures scheduled for March, the federation would have some time to identify a replacement if the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager leaves.



🚨 BREAKING: Manchester United have verbally agreed terms in principle with Mauricio Pochettino to become the new head coach.

Negotiations ongoing with US Federation to move forward as $10m release clause is available to get Poch.

Formal steps to follow — then here we go. https://t.co/y5hqUVv699— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 11, 2026



Guardiola emerges as the federation’s leading target



According to The Athletic, Guardiola would be a top target for U.S. Soccer if Pochettino departs. The former Manchester City boss has reportedly been discussed at several levels of the federation’s recruitment process, with officials prepared to explore the possibility of bringing him into international management for the first time.



The interest is not new, either. U.S. Soccer previously contacted Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp during its 2024 search before eventually appointing Pochettino, while former federation president Sunil Gulati has reportedly discussed the possibility of Guardiola coaching the national team in the past.



Pep Guardiola, Manager of Manchester City.



Guardiola has also spoken positively about the potential of American soccer. In 2024, he explained: “The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.”



The problem Guardiola would face with the USMNT



Despite his enthusiasm for the American project, Guardiola would face a significant tactical challenge that he rarely encountered during his decade at Manchester City: the limited time available to work with international players. At club level, he could spend weeks developing his system, repeating instructions and refining details on the training pitch, whereas national-team managers have only brief periods with their squads between international fixtures.



Guardiola is renowned for his meticulous approach and attention to detail, but attempting to transfer his usual methods directly to international soccer could prove difficult. As Bleacher Report’s assessment of a potential appointment pointed out, players could become overwhelmed by the volume of information and tactical instructions if the manager tried to replicate his club routines.



 Pep Guardiola, Manager of Manchester City, appears dejected



His success at Manchester City was also supported by an organization built around his footballing philosophy. The club had already established important connections with his Barcelona background through executives Txiki Begiristain and Ferran Soriano, helping create an environment in which Guardiola could implement his ideas over several seasons.



The USMNT would have to provide a different kind of support, particularly when preparing for major tournaments with limited training opportunities. His reputation alone would not guarantee that the American team could immediately reproduce the tactical standards he established at club level.



Another factor could could complicate the pursuit



There is another obstacle for U.S. Soccer: Guardiola’s uncertain plans after leaving Manchester City. The Catalan coach has repeatedly indicated that he wanted to step away from soccer management and spend time focusing on himself and his family. In July 2025, he told GQ that he intended to stop working after his City spell, explaining: “I don’t know how long I’ll stop, a year, two years, three years, five, ten, fifteen, I don’t know.”









The Spaniard also turned down the opportunity to take charge of Italy earlier in 2026. Italian soccer federation president Giovanni Malago explained his decision to La Repubblica: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”



U.S. Soccer could therefore face a difficult recruitment process even if the opportunity becomes available. The 55-year-old boss remains an attractive candidate, but the federation would need to convince him that the USMNT project is worth ending his break for while also adapting his demanding philosophy to the realities of international management.

items.title: Joao Felix’s brother casts doubt on the forward’s future alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Al Nassr
items.description:
Joao Felix’s future at Al Nassr, and his partnership with Cristiano Ronaldo, has come under a new question mark after comments from his younger brother. Hugo Felix, a 22-year-old midfielder who plays for Tondela, told Portuguese newspaper A Bola that the forward needs to return to Europe as soon as possible, a statement that could […] 
Joao Felix’s future at Al Nassr, and his partnership with Cristiano Ronaldo, has come under a new question mark after comments from his younger brother. 



Hugo Felix, a 22-year-old midfielder who plays for Tondela, told Portuguese newspaper A Bola that the forward needs to return to Europe as soon as possible, a statement that could add another layer of uncertainty about his stay at the Saudi club.



Hugo explained that he and Joao have already discussed the subject and that he gave him his opinion. He acknowledged that his brother is enjoying his time in Saudi Arabia and that he should keep playing with happiness and confidence, which he said have been clear since last season.



However, Hugo said that his brother needs to return to Europe in order to fulfill his dream. “He needs to return to Europe to play in a major league and in the Champions League, to stand out even more than he already does and, of course, to win the Champions League, because that is his dream,” the Tondela midfielder explained.




Simply unstoppable 🪄 pic.twitter.com/dpKoDa0ZBj— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) November 2, 2026




Al Nassr could be racing against the clock to keep Joao Felix



The reasons for Al Nassr’s urgency are not hard to find. Felix was a key piece in the club’s Saudi Pro League title last season, finishing with 26 goals and 18 assists in 47 matches across all competitions, and he has kept that level this campaign with seven goals and 10 assists in 14 appearances.


        


That production helps explain why the club’s directors have reportedly opened talks with his camp about prolonging his stay by two seasons, with a salary of €12.5 million per year (around $14.4 million), up from the current €10 million, according to Okaz.



The path to that renewal, however, is not as simple as signing a new contract. His current deal expires in June 2027, but it includes a clause that would let Al Nassr extend it unilaterally until 2029, although the club would have to pay Chelsea an additional €20 million to do so, according to Goal.



The same outlet reported that the club’s management is trying to move quickly to activate that option before a May deadline and to shut the door on Jorge Mendes, Felix’s agent, who would be hoping to take advantage of the expiring deal to move him to Barcelona on a free transfer or for a nominal fee.



Hugo Felix’s words, therefore, land at a sensitive time. Although they do not represent a decision, and the forward has not announced any plans to leave, they suggest that Joao could return to Europe at any time.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe set to miss France vs Italy clash in UEFA Nations League as Jose Mourinho connection to his absence emerges
items.description:
The Real Madrid forward’s latest fitness concern has also raised questions about his workload at club level, with Jose Mourinho potentially facing the consequences when the international break ends. 
Kylian Mbappe is facing another frustrating setback ahead of France’s crucial UEFA Nations League meeting with Italy, leaving Zinedine Zidane with a major selection headache. The Real Madrid forward’s latest fitness concern has also raised questions about his workload at club level, with Jose Mourinho potentially facing the consequences when the international break ends.



Mbappe did not participate in France’s final training session before Thursday’s encounter with Italy in Milan, according to reports from L’Equipe and Le Parisien. The 27-year-old instead received treatment from the national team’s medical staff after experiencing discomfort in his hamstring.



France’s coaching staff confirmed that the captain was receiving treatment but initially provided few details about the problem. Onda Cero also reported that the forward was working with physiotherapists and doctors, with further updates dependent on medical examinations.



According to L’Equipe, Mbappe is expected to miss the Italy fixture, although France hopes to have him available for Sunday’s meeting with Turkiye in Bordeaux. His absence would be a significant blow for Zidane, particularly with the national team looking to secure its position at the top of Nations League Group A1.



Kylian Mbappe of France.



Zidane calls up PSG forward as France deal with injuries



With Mbappe unlikely to feature against Italy, Zidane has called up Paris Saint-Germain forward Senny Mayulu to strengthen his attacking options. The 20-year-old had been training with France’s Under-21 squad before receiving his first senior-team call-up.



Les Blues already have several important players unavailable for the international fixtures. Inter striker Marcus Thuram and Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu are dealing with injuries, while Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni has also returned to Spain after suffering an adductor problem.



The timing is particularly unfortunate because France had welcomed Mbappe back after he missed their previous three matches through injury. He had scored the winning goal in Zidane’s first match in charge against Turkiye in September, but was forced off after experiencing pain in his left knee.



Senny Mayulu (PSG) rejoint l’Équipe de France dès cet après midi. https://t.co/0FtbhG5vCb— Equipe de France ⭐⭐ (@equipedefrance) November 11, 2026




Mourinho connection emerges as Mbappe’s workload raises concerns



The connection to Jose Mourinho comes through Mbappe’s demanding schedule at Real Madrid and the manager’s handling of the forward’s playing time. Despite his previous injury problems, the Frenchman has continued to play regularly for the Spanish club, featuring in almost the entire duration of recent matches.



According to the statistics included in the reports, the Frenchman played at least 84 minutes in each of Real Madrid’s eight consecutive victories. He completed the full 90 minutes in several of those matches, including games against Barcelona, Roma and Racing Santander, while also remaining on the pitch for 89 minutes against Valencia.



That workload has prompted questions about whether the forward has been given enough opportunities to rest, especially when Los Blancos had already established comfortable leads. The report highlighted matches against Racing Santander and Sevilla, in which Mbappe continued playing despite his team holding a three-goal advantage.



Kylian Mbappe of Real Madrid



Mourinho will therefore be hoping the latest hamstring problem proves minor, with Real Madrid preparing for a demanding period after the international break. The club reportedly faces six matches in 18 days, making Mbappe’s fitness particularly important.



When could Mbappe return?



France reportedly hopes Mbappe will recover in time to face Turkiye on Sunday, November 15. His decision to remain with the national team rather than immediately return to Madrid has offered some encouragement, although his availability will depend on how he responds to treatment.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo learns new date for Al-Nassr’s rescheduled AFC Champions League clash vs Al-Wasl, but unexpected twist emerges
items.description:
heir postponed AFC Champions League Elite meeting with Al-Wasl. However, fresh reports suggest that a surprise twist has emerged before the rearranged match can be treated as fully settled. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr have received an important update regarding their postponed AFC Champions League Elite meeting with Al-Wasl, with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) moving closer to settling the fixture’s new date. However, fresh reports suggest that a surprise twist has emerged before the rearranged match can be treated as fully settled.



The game was originally scheduled for October 26 but was postponed after Al-Wasl encountered difficulties travelling to Saudi Arabia. The delay sparked controversy, particularly after Saudi officials maintained that the necessary arrangements to host the fixture had already been completed.



The meeting is important for both clubs as they look to improve their positions in the West Zone. Al-Nassr currently sits seventh with six points from three matches, while Al-Wasl occupies 11th place with three points.



For Ronaldo’s side, the home fixture offers a chance to earn valuable points and strengthen its position in the league phase. Al-Wasl, meanwhile, will be eager to recover from its difficult start and move closer to the qualification places.



Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr celebrates scoring



The scheduling would also give both teams additional time to prepare for a match that was originally expected to take place several weeks earlier. Nevertheless, the latest development suggests that the announcement may not be the final word on the matter.



AFC identifies new date for Al-Nassr vs Al-Wasl



According to Voice of Emirates and Saudi newspaper Arriyadiyah, the AFC has confirmed December 27, 2026, as the proposed new date for the postponed encounter. The match is expected to take place at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh, with kick-off scheduled for 7:00 PM Saudi time, equivalent to 8:00 PM in the UAE.



The fixture was initially due to be played on October 26 as part of the AFC Champions League Elite’s West Zone league phase. However, Al-Wasl’s travel and logistical problems prevented the UAE side from reaching Riyadh, forcing the continental governing body to postpone the meeting.



The decision attracted criticism from the Saudi side, with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF) reportedly arguing that preparations had been completed. These included arrangements for flight permits, organizational support and coordination with Al-Wasl, while match officials had already arrived in Riyadh.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



What’s the twist regarding AFC’s proposed date?



According to Saudi journalist Khalid Al-Rashid, Al-Nassr will issue an official response regarding the revised date proposed for the match against Al-Wasl. This is the unexpected twist surrounding the announcement, as the Saudi club’s position on the suggested scheduling remains an important part of the latest developments.



Some reports have also mentioned December 28 as a possible alternative, creating uncertainty over whether December 27 will ultimately remain the agreed date. The distinction matters because the initial announcement presented December 27 as confirmed, while the subsequent update describes the date as a proposal awaiting Al-Nassr’s response.



The original postponement had already created tension between the parties, particularly following the disagreement over the circumstances that prevented Al-Wasl from travelling to Riyadh. Al-Nassr’s forthcoming statement could therefore provide further clarity on the arrangements and whether the club accepts the proposed schedule.

items.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
items.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managersMail us with all of your questions and answers“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. items.title: Arsene Wenger reportedly considers challenging Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency
items.description:
Arsene Wenger could emerge as an unexpected challenger to Gianni Infantino in the next FIFA presidential election. The former Arsenal manager is reportedly considering putting himself forward as a candidate, although he has not made a final decision, according to reports from the BBC. Wenger, 77, has worked at FIFA as chief of global football […] 
Arsene Wenger could emerge as an unexpected challenger to Gianni Infantino in the next FIFA presidential election. The former Arsenal manager is reportedly considering putting himself forward as a candidate, although he has not made a final decision, according to reports from the BBC.



Wenger, 77, has worked at FIFA as chief of global football development since 2019, a role that has given him close knowledge of the organization and would make him a formidable opponent for Infantino. French outlet L’Équipe, meanwhile, reported over the weekend that he is “tempted” to run and has been deliberating for several weeks.



Behind the idea is UEFA, which is reportedly looking for a credible alternative to Infantino after the summer controversy over his plan to sell a minority stake in a World Cup company to private investors.



Three continental confederations rejected the proposal, including UEFA, and Infantino eventually abandoned it, but the European body said it had lost confidence in the Swiss.



FIFA President, Gianni Infantino and Arsene Wenger talk following the FIFA Women’s Champions Cup 2026 Final. (Getty Images)



Even so, nothing is settled. Wenger has not yet formally entered the race, and he is not yet seen as UEFA’s preferred candidate, as other names are still being evaluated, while his age could also raise questions about whether he can lead FIFA for a full four-year term.



Key dates in the race for the FIFA presidency


        


Infantino has already confirmed that he will seek re-election, as a FIFA spokesperson told AFP in September. The Swiss-Italian became president in 2016, succeeding Sepp Blatter, and was re-elected without opposition in 2019 and 2023, so a rival such as Wenger would turn this vote into the first real contest of his tenure in a decade.



Candidates have until Nov. 18 to submit their nominations, which must be backed by at least five member associations, while the vote itself is scheduled for March 18, 2027, at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco. Japan’s Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy on Nov. 5, is the only declared challenger for now, although UEFA is expected to hold meetings this week to define who it will back.



That decision will be key because Infantino has been rallying support from Africa, Asia, Oceania, South America and the Caribbean Football Union, which leaves any opponent with little room to maneuver. In that sense, what UEFA and Wenger decide in the coming days will determine whether the election ends up with a credible alternative or with a campaign that barely changes the picture.

items.title: Ronald Araujo on Argentina without Lionel Messi: ‘We’re going to take advantage of that’
items.description:
Uruguay’s Ronald Araujo has sent a warning to Argentina ahead of a friendly at La Bombonera, where the Albiceleste will play without Lionel Messi for the first time. 
Argentina is set to begin a new chapter without Lionel Messi, and its first opponent is already treating that absence as an opportunity. The Albiceleste will face Uruguay on Friday, Nov. 13, at La Bombonera, in the first friendly of a FIFA window that is also the first since Messi retired from international play.



Uruguay defender Ronald Araujo, who was called up by coach Diego Forlan for this window, did not hide his intentions upon arriving in Montevideo. “In the end, they lost the best player in the world, and we’re going to take advantage of that,” he told reporters at the airport.



Even so, the Liverpool defender acknowledged the quality of the opponent. “They have great players, young players with a lot of quality, they’re a great power,” he said. Araujo also tempered his words with a dose of caution. “All matches against Argentina are difficult, but we’re going to show our football and keep growing as a national team,” he added, a message that carries extra weight for a Uruguay side looking to bounce back from a disappointing cycle under Marcelo Bielsa.



The Uruguayan also looked back at the last time his side won at La Bombonera, when Uruguay beat an Argentina led by Messi 2-0 in World Cup qualifiers in November 2023, with a goal from Araujo himself. “It was an unforgettable night for all of us, and hopefully we can repeat it,” he concluded.



Ronald Araujo celebrates a goal for Uruguay vs Argentina at La Bombonera. (Getty Images)



Argentina will leave Messi’s No. 10 shirt unused in this FIFA window



Argentina will not assign the No. 10 to any player in its friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica, according to Argentine outlet TyC Sports, in a decision reportedly made by coach Lionel Scaloni.


        


The gesture is possible because FIFA does not require consecutive numbering in friendlies, something that will not be the case in official tournaments. Since FIFA rules require World Cup and Copa America squad lists to be numbered from 1 to 26, Argentina cannot leave the shirt unused or retire it in those competitions.



For now, the question of who will wear it next remains open. There is no clear heir yet, but young players such as Nico Paz, Thiago Almada and Franco Mastantuono are among the options, while established names such as Julian Alvarez, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez are also in the conversation.



The answer could arrive in March 2027, when the South American qualifiers for the 2030 World Cup are expected to begin. Until then, the shirt Messi wore for almost two decades will remain without an owner, a symbolic first step for Argentina in its new era.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr could reportedly win their ACL match against Al Wasl without even playing it
items.description:
Al Nassr reportedly wants the AFC to award it the points after its match against Al Wasl was postponed, a decision that could reshape its position in the West region standings. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr could be closer to picking up three points in the AFC Champions League Elite without kicking a ball. The Saudi side was due to host Al Wasl in Riyadh on Oct. 26, but the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) postponed the match just hours before kickoff, and Al Nassr is now reportedly pushing to be awarded the win.



The AFC announced the decision without giving a reason or a new date, and reports from Saudi sports outlet Gulf News said that Al Wasl decided against making the trip because of flight disruptions and a lack of available flights.



The Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF), however, said it had completed every arrangement to receive the UAE club, including flight permits, and that the match commissioner and the referees had already arrived in Riyadh.



Al Nassr has since taken its first formal step. According to Saudi newspaper Al Riyadiya, the club wrote to the AFC asking for the reasons behind the postponement and submitted documents that show the landing permits were secured, along with the flight number of the private aircraft Al Wasl had arranged before changing its decision.




Latest update on #ACLElite League Stage match between 🇸🇦 Al Nassr Club and 🇦🇪 Al Wasl FC.https://t.co/28elJ5kyll— #ACLElite | #ACLTwo (@TheAFCCL) October 25, 2026




The team reportedly intends to pursue all available legal procedures, in coordination with the SAFF, to be awarded the points. For its part, AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa told Al Riyadiya that the confederation’s specialist committees are studying the matter.



A game in hand that could change the West standings for Al Nassr


        


Al Nassr currently sits seventh in the West region standings with six points from two wins and one loss. It has scored nine goals and conceded seven, for a goal difference of +2. That record keeps it inside the top eight places in the table, but only by a thin margin.



Al Wasl is a direct rival in the fight for a spot in the knockout stages. The UAE club is 11th with three points from one win and two losses, and a goal difference of -2, leaving it three points behind Al Nassr and two below the cutoff for qualification.



AFC Elite Champions League Group B standings.



If the AFC were to award the points to Al Nassr, the Saudi side would climb to nine, tying Al Hilal, Esteghlal and Shabab Al Ahli, while also denying Al Wasl the chance to close the gap with a win that would take the UAE club to six, level with Al Nassr. 



Although the final order would depend on tiebreakers and on how the result is recorded, that margin could prove decisive for a team that has already lost once.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo could pay the price as Al-Nassr faces more fixtures, but the rest-day difference raises bigger questions
items.description:
Recent changes to the Saudi Pro League calendar have increased the pressure on the Riyadh club, while also raising questions about how fairly the workload is being distributed among its biggest rivals. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr are heading into a demanding stretch of the 2026-27 campaign, with several important matches now packed into the final weeks of the year. Recent changes to the Saudi Pro League calendar have increased the pressure on the Riyadh club, while also raising questions about how fairly the workload is being distributed among its biggest rivals.



The revised schedule brings major domestic encounters closer and leaves Al-Nassr juggling commitments across several competitions. However, the fixture list has also exposed a potential disadvantage that could become increasingly significant as the title race develops.



The Saudi Pro League has confirmed new dates for three postponed Matchday 9 fixtures. Al-Ahli will host Al-Nassr on November 20, 2026, at Alinma Bank Stadium in Jeddah, while Al-Riyadh vs Al-Hilal and Al-Ittihad vs Al-Shabab have both been moved to December 21.



The matches were initially postponed in October because of logistical and scheduling considerations, including player recovery periods. The calendar subsequently gained more flexibility after the AFC postponed the 2027 Asian Cup, which had originally been scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia between January and February.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr lifts the Saudi Pro League Trophy



The tournament will now be held in December 2027 and January 2028, allowing domestic football officials to reconsider the fixture calendar.



Ronaldo faces demanding end to 2026



The rearranged Al-Ahli fixture is an immediate challenge for Al-Nassr, with the Saudi Clasico brought forward by several months. The encounter could have significant implications for the title race, particularly as both clubs look to maintain their position among the league’s leading contenders.



Al-Nassr also has a busy schedule across November and December, with seven matches listed before the end of 2026, excluding any additional fixtures that may follow. Its commitments include Saudi Pro League games against Al-Hazem, Al-Qadsiah, Al-Shabab and Al-Fayha, as well as AFC Champions League Elite meetings with Al-Sadd and Al-Gharafa.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al-Nassr reacts during prize presentation the Saudi Super Cup final



The club is also scheduled to face Al-Kholood in the Saudi Super Cup semi-final on December 20, with a potential final against Al-Ahli or Al-Qadsiah three days later. A Riyadh derby against Al-Hilal is set for January 1, 2027, at Al-Awwal Park.



Al-Nassr’s heavier workload raises questions over recovery time



The bigger concern centers on the difference in recovery time between Al-Nassr and some of its domestic rivals. According to the official schedules, Al-Nassr is competing in four tournaments: the Saudi Pro League, King’s Cup, AFC Champions League Elite and Saudi Super Cup, while Al-Hilal is involved in three.



Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr celebrates scoring



Despite that heavier overall workload, the account claims that recent scheduling adjustments give Al-Hilal, Al-Ahli and Al-Ittihad more rest days between league matches than Al-Nassr. That has fueled debate among supporters about whether the fixture calendar gives every title contender a comparable opportunity to recover.



The distinction is important because Al-Nassr’s additional cup commitments mean its players must manage more matches across the season. Ronaldo, one of the club’s most important attacking figures, could be particularly affected if the tight schedule limits recovery time between demanding encounters.

items.title: Manchester United reportedly want to take Mauricio Pochettino from USMNT as Michael Carrick’s exit nears
items.description:
With Michael Carrick’s future in doubt after a dismal start in the Premier League, Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the favorite to take over at Old Trafford, but his departure from USMNT would come at a price. 
Manchester United may be about to change managers, and Mauricio Pochettino appears to be the name at the top of the list. According to ESPN, the club is ready to part ways with Michael Carrick, and the head coach of the U.S. men’s national team is the favored candidate to replace him at Old Trafford.



The reason is the team’s worst start in the Premier League. United have won only once in their first 10 league matches and sit one point above the bottom of the table, in the relegation zone, a position that has put the club’s executives under pressure. 



Carrick, 45, signed a two-year contract in the summer after guiding the club to Champions League qualification as interim manager, but he has won only one of the four games since the club gave him a reprieve last month.



Pochettino, 54, would not come cheap. He extended his contract with the U.S. Soccer Federation until 2030 in August, after leading the United States to the round of 16 at the World Cup, and he has an escape clause of $10 million that United would have to pay. 







The former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain coach has also interviewed for the United job on three previous occasions and is regarded as having the Premier League experience and personality needed to lift the club out of danger.



However, nothing is official yet. According to reports, the club’s chief executive, Omar Berrada, and director of football, Jason Wilcox, have recommended Carrick’s dismissal, and the final decision is expected at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.


        


Other names on the list



Pochettino is not the only name in the conversation. Eddie Howe is another candidate admired by United’s executives, and since he left Newcastle in the summer, he is available. Julian Nagelsmann also appears among the coaches currently without a job, after he left the German national team following the World Cup.



The list does not end there. Other reports point to Kieran McKenna, who was interviewed for the job in 2024, as an option for Old Trafford, while Antonio Conte and Unai Emery have also been linked with the job in recent months.



For now, though, Pochettino appears to have a slight edge over the rest of the candidates. Everything will depend on what happens in Monaco on Wednesday, when United’s decision-makers are expected to decide on Carrick’s future and begin to define who will take charge.

items.title: Football Daily | ‘Where the hell is Roy Keane!’ Fifty shades of great football debate
items.description:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Forget about Michael Carrick. Don’t dwell on Women’s Bigger Cup. Fret not about Pierre Sage. No, the big football story of the day is Big Website’s Ultimate 1-50, a rundown of the male footballers best associated with each squad number. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé.
 
 
 Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). The days of two substitutes who wore Nos 12 and 14. The days of a quarter of wine gums in your pocket and misty rain drifting across the floodlights and … oh my god Asamoah Gyan is wearing No 3 and playing up front. This is not a drill. Repeat this is not a drill. Burn it all down, the game’s gone.
 
 
 There is something about it all that does invoke strangely strong reactions, but every day is a school day. So, yes, there remains a hallowed aura around 1-11 but even some of the game’s greats – we’re looking at you Gerd Müller and Johan Cruyff – are best associated with numbers outside of the traditional undectet. And, as Jonathan Wilson brilliantly illustrates here, there’s a risk of being a bit Eurocentric when it comes to numbering – Argentina’s tactical evolution, for example, meant their traditional back four lines up 4, 2, 6, 3, with the No 5 in central midfield. Brazil too has No 5 as the defensive midfielder, with the standard back four as 4, 2, 3, 6. And don’t get us started on Hungary at Wembley in 1953 – Nandor Hidegkuti, you rascal! So do yourself a favour and dig into today’s offering. You might learn something. Or you might just get really, really cross about Curtis Jones. Either way, it’s win-win.Appreciate it’s all highly subjective but quite how you can give the all-time No 17 shirt to Kevin De Bruyne without so much as a mention of the legendary Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu is beyond me. What other player has gone from non-league to Premier League with the same club? OK, it’s a bit niche but a far more worthy winner in my completely unbiased (honest guv) opinion” – Kev Goddard.All this talk of 4-4 draws (yesterday’s Football Daily) is very intoxicating for Chesterfield fans of a certain vintage. First up, the 1992 draw at Anfield where we threw away a 4-1 lead after a Liverpool comeback inspired by Istvan Kozma (no, really). Dave Lancaster scored two that night and observed that he had thought beforehand there might be eight goals in it, but not that we’d score four of them. And then in 2004 at Saltergate against Grimsby, where we threw away a 3-2 lead to go 4-3 down, before equalising with a last-minute penalty thanks to David Reeves. The attendance that day was 4,444. Makes you think …” – David Ede.To stop managers continually going outside their technical areas, why not erect a ‘banners and poles’ surround, the sort of thing you see on pavements outside pubs and cafes? If the idea sounds a bit too simple, just mention the opportunity of more advertising space” – Peter Storch.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
items.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrateUltimate 1-50: check out our complete list of playersNumbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche, the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivien Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque.But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. Here’s our list and the stories behind itThe relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal retirement was not just about Jorge Jesus as journalist reveals whether CR7 could return under new coach
items.description:
Although his public fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus dominated the headlines, comments from a journalist close to the Al-Nassr star suggest there may be more to the story than a disagreement over playing time. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s decision to end his Portugal career has raised questions about whether the legendary forward could ever reconsider his international retirement. Although his public fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus dominated the headlines, comments from a journalist close to the Al-Nassr star suggest there may be more to the story than a disagreement over playing time.



With Ronaldo having spent 23 years representing his country, many supporters would welcome the opportunity to see him receive a more fitting farewell. However, the possibility of a return could depend on more than a change in the coaching staff.



Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, 2026, bringing an end to a Portugal career that produced 234 appearances and a record 146 goals. The announcement came after tensions with Jesus, who had previously coached the forward at Al-Nassr before taking charge of the national team.



The disagreement reportedly intensified during the September international break. Ronaldo started his nation’s 1-0 victory over Wales but was left on the bench throughout the subsequent match against Norway, despite warming up for an extended period.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal walks to the bench as a substitute



The situation eventually led to Ronaldo leaving the national team camp. The Portuguese Football Federation subsequently handed him a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine, while the forward later confirmed that he would no longer represent Portugal.



Jorge Jesus expected Ronaldo to return



Jesus maintained that he had intended to include Ronaldo in his plans for the November international fixtures and said he was unaware of the retirement decision before the public announcement. The Portugal coach also insisted that he felt no guilt over his decisions, arguing that he had acted in the team’s best interests.



The coaching staff and federation president Pedro Proenca reportedly attempted to persuade Ronaldo to reconsider. Their efforts were unsuccessful, leaving Portugal without its most prolific international goalscorer ahead of the next Nations League matches.



Would Ronaldo return if Portugal appointed a different coach?



Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda, who is close to Ronaldo, has now addressed whether the situation could change if Jesus eventually left his position. Asked whether the forward might have continued representing Portugal under a different coach, Sepulveda suggested that Ronaldo would have retired from international soccer regardless of who was in charge. “No, no, I think that in terms of playing for the national team, Ronaldo wouldn’t play again even if the coach were different,” Sepulveda explained.



Roberto Martinez, Head Coach of Portugal, speaks to players at the hydration break.



The journalist nevertheless indicated that the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure involved several factors and people. He suggested that the forward had wanted an opportunity to say goodbye to Portugal on his own terms, but the events surrounding his final appearances left him disappointed.



Sepulveda also suggested that Ronaldo felt many people wanted to see him continue playing for the national team. However, the situation had become complicated enough that simply replacing Jesus would not necessarily persuade the 41-year-old to reverse his decision.



Although Sepulveda does not expect Ronaldo to return as an active international player, his comments leave room for the possibility of a different kind of ending. He indicated that supporters may have to wait until Jesus leaves the national team before circumstances change sufficiently for a more fitting farewell to be considered.
